# Native Contact Source Closure

This provisional F07 calculation records a narrow, opt-in source declaration
for native sphere/half-space contact in constrained-muscle replay. It binds
OpenSim contact force and geometry components to the exact model bytes and
records native wrench observations. It does not add contact to any capture
model, establish ground calibration, qualify contact parameters, or establish
support, grip, physical validity, full-horizon replay, or scientific
qualification. Publication remains blocked.

## Exact Declaration and Executed Provider

The declaration is limited to `HuntCrossleyForce` and
`SmoothSphereHalfSpaceForce` with `ContactSphere` and `ContactHalfSpace`
geometry. Each force and geometry is identified by absolute component path,
concrete class, and the hash of its native component serialization. The
declaration also binds the full model SHA-256. Any changed model bytes or
force/geometry component invalidates the declaration. Unsupported contact
geometry and undeclared forces remain rejected.

The policy identity covers both the declaration and the code that executes it:
the source-bound contact policy/sampler and `opensim_force_torque.py`, which
provides native force and torque sampling. Constrained replay incorporates
that provider digest into its policy identity. Mutating the provider therefore
changes the identity even when model bytes and declaration data are unchanged.
The existing native wrench sampler remains shared with the legacy replay path;
this declaration does not introduce a second contact law.

Contact execution is available only when the caller supplies a valid typed
declaration. The default constrained path continues to reject contact-bearing
models. The declaration is not yet a request-level authorization for a
particular private capture, and it cannot override unrelated source, state,
constraint, or execution blockers.

## Evidence and Limits

OpenSim 4.6 synthetic fixtures exercise declared Smooth and Hunt-Crossley
source closure, the corresponding sphere and half-space geometry identities,
contact-free default rejection, source/component mutation rejection, and
finite native wrench output from a constrained Smooth-contact replay. Existing
legacy replay fixtures exercise both contact laws through the shared sampler.
The generated Hunt-Crossley source fixture is rejected by the strict
self-contained XML gate, so this evidence does not claim constrained
Hunt-Crossley replay.
These are bounded software tests. They do not establish that either law or
geometry is appropriate for a human capture, nor do they demonstrate a
contact-bearing full-body Moco solve or full-horizon independent replay.

Keep contact, support/grip, anatomy, passive physiology, capture matching,
full-horizon replay, and all-model parity unqualified. The calculation
registry remains empty and publication remains blocked.
